title: Shelves In Savoy Building Older Than Many Antiques On Sale
text:
Shelves In Savoy Building Older Than Many Antiques On Sale

SAVOY — The show cases that display a lot of the wares in Molly and Bridge's antique store here are older than many of the items on the shelves.

"This building was put up about 1900 and the shelves were built in," said E.L. Harden, a retired Amarillo school custodian who holds down the shop for his son, C.R., and J.C. Moore.

The antique store is the offspring of a collection started years ago by Moore. It finally overflowed his yard, located a half block south of the building he and the younger Harden rented, and the two men decided to open a store.

"They've been in business two years now," said the elder Harden. "My son is a truck driver and is on the road about three-four days a week. Moore is a housekeeper at Wilson N. Jones Hospital in Sherman."

"They've given me the authority to buy as well as sell, but I have to be pretty confident I can move an item before I'll buy it," he said.

Harden said the store has "a little of everything. There ought to be something here for everyone who comes in."

Rollop desks are all the rage these days. There's one tucked away in a corner in pretty fair shape. How about a tredle sewing machine? Remember the old GE refrigerators with the motor on top? Or a blacksmith forge and anvil hardly used.

Coke used to be better when it came in metal cases. There is a stack of those oldies handy. How about a 1921 crank model cash register? "Put a roll of tape in it and she's ready to go. That old register is as good as new," Harden said.

Harden reached high up on a shelf and pulled down an old kerosene lamp with a black onyx base.

"This lamp is more than 150 years old," and Harden said if you take the base screws off and you've got the bowl, wick and chimney left.

There was a large box about half full of assorted buttons. "I sell 'em a penny each," said Harden. "In the last two years I've sold more than $60 worth. Yeah," he said, "Some of them might have had a much higher value, but the buyer wasn't about to tell me about it."

Harden said he was glad he wasn't still on the school job. "Kids have changed too much for me," he said. "Their hair style, dress style and even their attitude is different. It isn't like it used to be."

Harden occupies a rocker in the front of one of the two buildings that houses the antiques and junk. He's right in front of the entrance door; The second building's outside door is kept locked and entry is gained through an adjoining door.

"The corner building originally was a drug store and the second building originally was a drug store 75 years ago," he said.

[Photograph caption:] 150-YEAR-OLD LAMP — Savoy Antique Dealer E. L. Harden holds up an old kerosene lamp he says is 150 years old. It has an onyx base that screws off.
notes: Feature article about an antique store in Savoy. The shop name 'Molly and Bridge's' appears in the lede.
